fyNote: Financial year ends 31 December. 1H = January to June; 2026 figures are unaudited. Valuation uses the last 12 months (July 2025 to June 2026). Next results: Q3 2026, due late November 2026.

sources.title: IHH interim financial report, half-year to 30 June 2026

segmentNote: Hospitals in five home markets earn almost all revenue; Turkiye and Europe is the largest (Q2 p.16).

how.title: How IHH makes money
how.text: Revenue = patients treated (hospital stays and outpatient visits) x average bill per patient

story.scale_label: plus clinics and labs, in 10 countries

items.label: Staff costs
items.tip: Salaries for doctors, nurses and hospital staff, the biggest cost.

items.label: Medicines and consumables
items.tip: Drugs, implants, surgical supplies and other materials used on patients.

items.label: Other operating costs
items.tip: Utilities, maintenance, short leases, bad debts and other running costs.

items.label: Purchases and contracted services
items.tip: Outside services such as specialists, cleaning, catering and lab work.

items.label: Depreciation and amortisation
items.tip: Wear and tear on hospital buildings and medical equipment.

items.label: Tax
items.tip: Income tax; doubled in 1H2026, partly from Turkiye's high-inflation accounting.

items.label: Partners' share of profit
items.tip: Profit belonging to minority shareholders, for example in Fortis and Parkway Life REIT.

items.label: Profit to shareholders
items.tip: What is left for shareholders: paid as dividends or kept to grow the business.

pnl.incomeNote: Plus about RM5.70 per RM100 of revenue from other income, interest and an accounting gain from Turkiye's high inflation.

fiveYear.note: Full years. Core profit without one-offs (RM million): 2021 1,595 · 2022 1,381 · 2023 1,280 · 2024 1,685 · 2025 1,818. First half 2026: revenue RM13.6bn (+8%), profit RM1,101m (+15%).

rows.name: Turkiye and Europe (Acibadem)
rows.tip: Acibadem hospitals in Turkiye and Europe; the biggest market by revenue.

rows.name: Singapore (Mount Elizabeth, Gleneagles)
rows.tip: Premium hospitals with the highest bill per patient.

rows.name: India (Fortis, Gleneagles)
rows.tip: IHH completed its offer for more Fortis shares in November 2025.

rows.name: Greater China
rows.tip: Hospitals and clinics in Hong Kong and Shanghai; still loss-making.

rows.name: Labs (diagnostic laboratories)
rows.tip: Blood tests and other lab services.

rows.name: Parkway Life REIT
rows.tip: Owns hospital and nursing-home buildings and rents them out.

segments.note: Half-year to 30 June 2026. Profit by segment before head-office costs, eliminations and the Turkiye hyperinflation adjustment (Q2 p.16).

assets.label: Money owed by patients and insurers

balance.note: More than a quarter of what IHH owns is goodwill: the premium it paid when buying hospital groups such as Acibadem and Fortis. Borrowings were trimmed slightly in the first half of 2026.

cash.wfNote: In the first half of 2026 the hospitals generated RM2.4bn of cash, which paid for RM1.6bn of new capacity, dividends and some debt repayment.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM70.1 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM31 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 dividends)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM1.3 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM41 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 2.2 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM7 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin 1H2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM8.10.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.plain: Borrowings minus cash: RM13.77 billion owed to lenders after using all its cash.

metrics.label: Net gearing
metrics.plain: Net debt is 39% of shareholders' funds. Under 50% is usually seen as comfortable; above 100% means lenders fund more than owners.

metrics.label: Free cash flow 1H2026
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM771 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

metrics.label: Core profit FY2025
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders without one-off items such as deferred tax changes and property revaluations: up 8% (AR p.50).

drivers.evidence: Demand stays resilient on demographics, health awareness and complex care (Q2 p.28)
drivers.why: Long-term demand for hospital care keeps growing.

drivers.evidence: Revenue up 8% in 1H2026 to RM13.6bn; average bills rose in every market in 2025 (Q2 p.2; AR p.20)
drivers.why: Higher-value treatments lift revenue per patient.

drivers.evidence: More than 1,400 operational beds added in FY2025 (AR p.51)
drivers.why: More capacity means more patients, once new wards fill up.

drivers.evidence: Bought hospitals in Turkiye and India; Fortis offer completed November 2025 (AR p.51; Q2 p.11)
drivers.why: Adds hospitals quickly, but costs cash.

drivers.evidence: Middle East tensions led some foreign patients to defer elective procedures (Q2 p.28)
drivers.why: Hits premium hospitals that serve foreign patients; management says the impact is limited.

drivers.evidence: Insurers, corporate payors and regulators focus on affordability and usage (Q2 p.28)
drivers.why: Limits how fast prices can rise.

drivers.evidence: Staff costs +10% in 1H2026, faster than revenue; pressure from consumables, drugs and utilities (Q2 p.2, p.28)
Multi-year transformation: technology, digitalisation and productivity programmes (Q2 p.28)
Tax doubled to RM606m in 1H2026, partly linked to Turkiye's hyperinflation accounting (Q2 p.2, p.16)
drivers.why: Lowers profit even as the hospitals do well.

drivers.evidence: RM365m accounting gain from hyperinflation in 1H2026 (Q2 p.2)
drivers.why: Makes reported profit swing; investors look at core profit too.

drivers.evidence: Management flags exposure to currency moves against the ringgit (Q2 p.28)
drivers.why: Most revenue is earned outside Malaysia.

drivers.evidence: FY2025 dividend raised to 10.5 sen (AR p.51)
drivers.why: Signals confidence in steady cash flow.

drivers.evidence: About 31 times last-12-month profit at RM7.93 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: Investors pay a premium for a defensive, growing business; slower growth would hurt.

suppliers: Staff costs are the biggest cost: RM5.5bn in 1H2026; wage inflation is a key pressure
Medicines, implants and consumables used on patients
Outside services such as specialist, cleaning, catering and laboratory work
Electricity and water; scanners, surgical robots and other medical technology
customers: Local patients across 10 countries; Turkiye and Europe is the biggest market by revenue
Pay many hospital bills; focused on affordability and controlling usage
Set healthcare rules and pay for some public schemes
Foreign patients; some delayed elective treatment because of Middle East tensions
supply.note: The reports describe these groups but do not give a revenue share for each payor type or name individual suppliers.

competitors.name: KPJ Healthcare, Sunway Healthcare, Columbia Asia
competitors.source: General market knowledge, not the report

outlook.text: Demand for quality healthcare remains resilient, supported by demographics and demand for complex care (Q2 p.28).
Multi-year transformation programmes expected to improve efficiency and support margins (Q2 p.28).
Management is 'cautiously optimistic' about delivering sustainable growth (Q2 p.28).
Cost pressures (wages, consumables, drugs, utilities), insurer pressure, Middle East tensions and currency moves (Q2 p.28).

outlookOverall.text: Management is cautiously optimistic, citing resilient demand and a diversified network (Q2 p.28).
